title_en: Interim Provisions on Strengthening the Administration of Cooperative Publishing with Foreign Countries

articles.content_en: I. Cooperative publication with foreign parties must be in conformity with China's foreign policy and diplomatic guidelines, conducive to strengthening external propaganda and cultural exchange; shall not impair China's sovereignty and national interests; and must strictly comply with the state provisions on confidentiality.

II. In cooperative publication with foreign parties, attention shall be paid to understanding the international book market, safeguarding the rights and interests of Chinese authors and publishers, and achieving economic gains on the basis of equality and mutual benefit.
III. The determination of foreign cooperative projects shall be based on one's own conditions and characteristics, and shall conform to the publishing policy and scope of the publishing house.

IV. Foreign cooperative publication projects shall be determined through full consultation between both parties. The editorial policy, content of the manuscript, and the final version of the cooperative publication shall all be subject to the consent of our side. No manuscript that has been reviewed and approved by our side may be altered, added to, or deleted by the other party without our consent. Photographs used in photographic albums or other publications introducing China's situation under cooperative publication shall generally be provided by our side, and it shall be inappropriate to adopt the method of sending personnel from the other party to take photographs or joint photography.

V. Manuscripts edited by foreign parties for cooperative publication for use by Chinese readers shall be those urgently needed by China, and where necessary, the content thereof shall be added to, deleted from, or adapted in accordance with China's circumstances, and economically, efforts shall be made to avoid using foreign exchange to pay the remuneration due to the other party.

VI. Cooperative publication with foreign parties may only be carried out by publishing houses formally approved by the state. No non-publishing entity or individual may engage in cooperative publication with foreign parties. Without the consent of the original publishing house, no publishing house may cooperate with foreign parties to publish books or periodicals published by other publishing houses. For manuscripts that a publishing house intends to publish in cooperation with foreign parties, the consent of the original author or the original editorial unit shall be obtained in advance.

VII. Publishing houses may directly negotiate cooperative publication business with foreign parties, or may entrust specialized companies approved by the state to engage in foreign cooperative publication business, or reliable foreign agents, to carry out such business.

VIII. The entities engaging in cooperative publication with our side shall be friendly to us and have reliable reputation and funds, and contracts shall not be signed with foreign businessmen whose circumstances are unclear.

IX. To clarify the rights and obligations of both parties, a contract with a definite term shall be signed for each cooperative project. The ownership of copyright, the transfer or licensing of the right to publish and distribute and other rights by one party to the other, and the amount, method, and time of payment of remuneration shall all be specified item by item in the contract. No manuscript or picture provided by our side may be transferred in copyright, have the right of use expanded, or have the distribution territory expanded by the other party without our consent.

XI. For the necessary exchanges between business personnel and foreign parties in carrying out foreign cooperative publication, the competent authorities shall simplify the examination and approval formalities and provide convenience to facilitate the smooth implementation of contracts.

XIII. In the work of foreign cooperative publication, publishing houses shall promote the style of socialist cooperation, pay attention to the exchange of information, maintain external coordination, and in case of differences and conflicts, they shall conduct internal consultation or report to the higher authority for coordination and resolution.
XIV. In foreign exchanges, the foreign affairs discipline shall be strictly observed, and national dignity and state reputation shall be safeguarded.
